% Shared normative core: definitions
\section{Normative scientific definitions}
\label{sec:definitions}

\subsection{Method, estimand, and fit boundary}

\ContractID{} is an optimal matched-template amplitude estimator only under
the exact criterion and premises in Section~\ref{sec:optimality}. It publishes
a filtered amplitude map. At each fixed parent-pixel anchor it performs a
fixed-template, fixed-anchor, one-parameter linear amplitude estimate. It does
not select candidates, optimize position, fit morphology or background,
deblend, infer source existence, or produce a catalog. It is neither
posterior/Wiener sky reconstruction nor ordinary source-shaped convolution.

Each realization has the immutable scientific identity
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
(method\_id, estimand, parent\_id, parent\_class, anchor\_lattice,
WCS/frame, template\_id, requested/effective/resolved/applied/realized
generation, weighting\_object, exact\_operator, realized\_operator,
numerical\_profile, response\_family, support\_family, units/calibration,
covariance\_scope, NOI\_lifecycle, product\_bundle, validity,
failure\_policy, provenance).
\end{quote}
A scientifically consequential change creates a new realization, generation,
or separately named method. A representation-only change that exactly
preserves the scientific object and supported query vocabulary does not change
the estimand or scientific generation.

\subsection{Parent classes and anchor lattice}

Exactly one parent class is admitted per application: one immutable normalized
ordinary-MAP observation bundle, or one immutable normalized ordinary-MAP
coadd bundle with its exact contributing-observation membership. They are
distinct applications. This contract asserts no filter/coadd commutation and
owns no coaddition. JINC and other derived parents are not admitted. Numerical
computability cannot repair missing MAP authority.

The base-v0.1 owner disposition places one output anchor at every exact parent
ordinary-MAP pixel center. The output amplitude field preserves the parent's
WCS, frame, grid, shape, indexing, order, phase origin, and pixel-center
convention, except that exact support rules may make anchors unavailable. No
interpolation is part of anchor creation. Template translation at an anchor,
including even/odd sampling and ties, follows the exact deterministic template
object. Subpixel, oversampled, and independent output lattices are successors.

\subsection{Template-response scientific object}

Each application binds one immutable template-response scientific object,
declared outside target, source, candidate, population, and NOI-member
learning. It binds the unit-amplitude convention, source-domain reference,
parent response, anchor/WCS relation, sampling, phase, support, CAL/BEAM
lineage, validity, generation, and supported query vocabulary.

The same scientific object may be represented by exact materialization, an
exact structured form, or exact lineage/query reconstruction. A
representation-only change shall preserve every supported query and shall not
alter the amplitude estimand. Template mismatch is not silently absorbed into
normalization or parent covariance.

\subsection{Five support roles}
\label{sec:support-roles}

The following supports are distinct:
\begin{description}
\item[$\Supp_{\rm apply}(p)$.] Exact parent payload rows with nonzero
coefficients in $L_{p,g}$. Exact-zero coefficients neither require nor
dereference their payloads.
\item[$\Supp_{\rm template}(p)$.] Exact rows and metadata required to define or
query $t_p$.
\item[$\Supp_{\rm state}(g)$.] Complete population influencing learned
covariance, spectra, reliability, window, rank, null, regularization, or other
resolved state.
\item[$\Supp_{\rm response}(p,s)$.] Exact state, template, and operator support
required by the declared response query.
\item[$\Supp_{\rm store}$.] Representation footprint. It has no scientific
authority and may change losslessly.
\end{description}
An output anchor is admitted only when complete application support is present
and valid. No partial-support estimator, edge renormalization, extension,
imputation, background subtraction, learned taper, or signal-derived support
belongs to this method. Numerical fill is allowed only after exact erosion
proves zero application coefficient. Causal provenance retains
$\Supp_{\rm state}$ even when a fixed-state derivative touches only
$\Supp_{\rm apply}$.

\subsection{Weighting and local covariance order}

$W_p$ is the selected frozen complete bilinear weight, exactly self-adjoint and
positive semidefinite. A parent coefficient has only its selected-route role;
its name, positivity, units, reciprocal, or diagonal placement does not make
it covariance, precision, or inverse variance.

Local GLS first restricts the authorized parent covariance:
$C_p=E_pC_{\rm parent}E_p^{\mathsf T}$, then inverts it only on the exact
declared local estimable subspace. In general
\[
 (E_pC_{\rm parent}E_p^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
 \ne E_pC_{\rm parent}^{-1}E_p^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Using a global-precision subblock conditions on outside data and is a different
method with a different influence domain, response, covariance, and edge rule.

\subsection{Learn--Resolve--Apply state graph}
\label{sec:state-graph}

State advances through three explicit operations:
\begin{description}
\item[Learn.] Derive candidate covariance, spectral/reliability information,
window, rank, null, regularization, and diagnostics from one declared
population, with source/target protection and state uncertainty recorded.
\item[Resolve.] Select one owner-authorized \AO{001} method and bind its
parameters, support, scientific identity, numerical-conformance policy,
failure disposition, and immutable generation. Externally declared state
enters here without observational learning.
\item[Apply.] Use the resolved state unchanged. No target, candidate, source,
or NOI-member update occurs during Apply.
\end{description}
Requested, effective, learned-candidate, resolved, applied, realized, and
published identities are distinct even when their values happen to agree.
Observation and coadd states are separate. A compatible NOI member receives
the identical resolved transformation, support, normalization, and failure
rules. Any update creates a successor; per-member relearning is a different
future method.

\subsection{Fixed-state, full-procedure, realized, and reference response}
\label{sec:response-families}

The fixed-state response is
$R_{\rm fixed}(p,s)=L_{p,g_0}t_s^{\rm full}$. It may be asymmetric,
anisotropic, nonstationary, position-dependent, or nonlocal. A learned
procedure has a separately typed full-procedure response obtained only by an
authorized exact rerun or finite-difference definition that reruns Learn and
Resolve after perturbation. The state-change record is retained separately.
Until such authority exists, $R_{\rm FP}$ is \Unavailable{}; no FLT, FRUIT,
SRC, or other consumer may call $R_{\rm fixed}$ the full-procedure response.

When the produced amplitude field uses a realized operator $\widetilde L$,
its actual response is $R_{\rm realized}=\widetilde LT$. The exact scientific
comparator is $R_{\rm reference}=LT$. These are not interchangeable.

\subsection{Product roles and atomic lifecycle}
\label{sec:product-roles}

The required atomic signal bundle contains the filtered amplitude field plus
its quantity/unit, parent and anchor-lattice identity, template convention,
resolved and realized operator/state identity, application validity, actual
response reference, uncertainty availability, lifecycle, and complete
provenance. Failure of any required member prevents a complete publication
candidate.

Independently atomic qualified companions may carry authorized covariance,
frozen-NOI uncertainty, response, or exact state/lineage. Every companion has
its own scientific identity, support, population, unit, validity, lifecycle,
and named-use policy. Optional failure does not change the signal estimand.
No numerator, denominator, kernel, field-power estimate, response slice,
inverse scale, standardized field, or intermediate is a public science product
without a complete role and policy.

\subsection{Lifecycle vocabulary}
\label{sec:lifecycle}

\begin{longtable}{p{0.25\linewidth}p{0.65\linewidth}}
\toprule
State & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endhead
\NotRequested{} & No request exists. This is not disabled. \\
\Requested{} & A named method/product/use was requested; no admission is yet
implied. \\
\Effective{} & Boundary resolution determined that the request applies to
this parent and method identity. \\
\Disabled{} & An applicable requested route was explicitly disabled by its
authorized state or policy. \\
\Unavailable{} & A required authority, input, option, support, or scientific
premise is absent; no numerical value is asserted. \\
\Resolved{} & Method, state, parameters, support, policy, and failure
disposition are immutable for the generation. \\
\Applied{} & The resolved operator was invoked on an admitted parent. \\
\Complete{} & Every required member and predicate exists and the bundle is
eligible for publication; this is not publication, validation, or readiness. \\
\Realized{} & The declared numerical operator produced the immutable product
values and their actual response/covariance identities. \\
\Failed{} & An authorized attempt began but a required operation or closure
check failed. \\
\NotProduced{} & Policy intentionally produced no artifact after a valid
disposition; it is not zero or unavailable. \\
\Superseded{} & An immutable successor exists under an authorized policy; the
predecessor is retained and never rewritten. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{SCI-VAL named-use evaluation}

SCI-VAL evaluates an owner-approved named-use profile. It retains four
independent axes: request, applicability, eligibility, and realization. FLT
owns the producer facts, dependency graph, named-use disposition, prescribed
consumer action, and failure semantics. VAL registers and evaluates; it does
not filter, publish, select an option, invent a missing fact, or perform
observational/scientific validation. Each profile keeps separate verdicts for
parent admission (PA), state admission (SA), signal publication (SP),
conditional-covariance use (CU), NOI-companion use (NU), response-companion
publication/use (RU), and FLT-to-FRUIT producer-envelope use (FH).

\subsection{First-class FLT-to-FRUIT producer envelope}

The FLT product contract preserves a first-class interface sufficient for a
future FRUIT method to consume the filtered amplitude product without
reconstructing undocumented FLT implementation state. At minimum it identifies
the filtered quantity, template, response, valid support, units/calibration,
method/state identity, uncertainty availability, and provenance. Additional
FLT state required by an authorized FRUIT method remains exactly available or
reconstructable through product lineage. FLT does not guess the future query
vocabulary and defines no FRUIT model, recurrence, subtraction/add-back,
learning, stopping, restart, selection, response, uncertainty, or
interpretation.

\subsection{Producer ownership and claim layers}

MAP owns the immutable parent identity, support, response, covariance, beam,
calibration, WCS, lifecycle, and provenance. The template producer owns the
unit-amplitude response object. CAL/BEAM owns calibration and beam authority.
FLT owns the exact transformation, resolved state, actual response/covariance
consequences, products, lifecycle, and one-way producer envelope. NOI owns its
realization population and empirical uncertainty meaning. FRUIT owns any
future FRUIT science. No SRC boundary is created.

Scientific authority, implementation conformity, representation fidelity,
observational/scientific validation, achieved performance, readiness, and
production are separate claims. This draft establishes none beyond its own
proposed scientific text.
